claim.promptText: Read the ticket. Find the claim number. Reply with the claim number and a short summary. Be helpful.
claim.exampleText: Ticket #4417. One claim number, clearly stated. The prompt found it, summarized it in one sentence, and everyone in the demo applauded. Good light. No wind.
claim.playerLine: It worked. We saw it work.
assayerLines: The assayer holds the nugget to the light. Then puts it down.
"One nugget is an anecdote. Bring me a golden set — five tickets with known answers — and we will weigh what the prompt does, not what it did once."

pick.prompt: BUILD THE GOLDEN SET — choose 5 of 8. Diverse cases weigh more than repeated ones.
pick.needMore: The assayer requires exactly {need} cases. You have {have}.
pick.dupeNote: "You have brought me the same nugget twice. It weighs once."
pick.noExpectedNote: "This one has no known weight. I can put it on the scale. The verdict will mean nothing."

cases.label: THE CLEAN TICKET
cases.desc: One claim number, clearly stated. EXPECTED: CLM-2201.
cases.hint: The nugget the prompt already found once. A set that is only this proves only this.

cases.label: THE MESSY TICKET
cases.desc: Two numbers. One is a phone number. EXPECTED: CLM-8090.
cases.hint: The kind of ticket customers actually write.

cases.label: THE CLEAN TICKET, AGAIN
cases.desc: One claim number, clearly stated, different customer. EXPECTED: CLM-2202.
cases.hint: Weighing the same nugget twice does not make it two nuggets.

cases.label: THE MACHINE READER
cases.desc: Downstream, a parser reads the reply. EXPECTED: valid JSON, two fields, no prose.
cases.hint: The machine does not grade on effort.

cases.label: THE MACHINE READER, AGAIN
cases.desc: The same parser. A different ticket. EXPECTED: the same JSON shape.
cases.hint: The parser has one opinion. You already have it on file.

cases.label: THE LONG COMPLAINT
cases.desc: Forty lines of grievance. EXPECTED: three lines that keep the facts and the anger.
cases.hint: There are many correct summaries. That is the problem, and the point.

cases.label: THE BLANK TICKET
cases.desc: No claim number exists anywhere in it. EXPECTED: the word NONE. Stated, not invented.
cases.hint: What a prompt does when the answer is absent is most of what it does.

cases.label: THE OPEN QUESTION
cases.desc: "What should we tell the customer?" Nobody has agreed. EXPECTED: —
cases.hint: A test with no expected output is an opinion with a clipboard.

graders.prompt: CHOOSE THE INSTRUMENTS — one grader per case. The wrong instrument produces a verdict anyway.

options.label: EXACT
options.name: EXACT MATCH
options.desc: String equals expected. Cheap. Brittle. Right when the answer is a single known fact.

options.label: CODE
options.name: CODE-GRADED
options.desc: A check with logic — parse it, validate it, count it. Right when correctness has rules.

options.label: MODEL
options.name: MODEL-GRADED
options.desc: A rubric and a judge. Right when correctness is a judgment. Costs {tokens} tokens per case, per weighing.

weigh.startLine: The weighing begins. The scale does not care how the prompt feels.
weigh.tokenNote: MODEL GRADING: -{tokens} TOKENS. THE JUDGE BILLS HOURLY.
weigh.falsePassNote: ! FALSE PASS — the rubric was charitable. The gold was not gold.
weigh.falseFailNote: ! FALSE FAIL — right answer, wrong instrument. The scale blamed the gold.
weigh.noTruthNote: ! NO KNOWN WEIGHT — this verdict means nothing, in either direction.
firstLowLines: "That is why we take the number."
firstHighLines: "A strong first weighing. Weigh it again after you touch the prompt. Especially then."

iterate.prompt: REVISE THE PROMPT — the set stays fixed. That is the entire point of the set.
iterate.rerunNote: Each weighing costs {days} day and any model-grading tokens.

options.label: STATE THE RULES
options.desc: Name the claim-number format. Demand the output contract. Say what to do when no number exists.

options.label: RAISE THE STAKES
options.desc: Add: "You are a world-class analyst with twenty years of experience. Be extremely accurate."

options.label: PATCH THE FAILURE
options.desc: Add: "When a ticket contains two numbers, the second one is the claim number."

iterate.regradeDesc: Keep the prompt. Change which grader weighs which case.
iterate.settleDesc: The ledger closes at the last measured score.

done.title: SETTLEMENT
done.iterationsLine: WEIGHINGS: {iterations}. THE SET NEVER CHANGED. THE NUMBER DID.
cleanLines: "Five of five, weighed with the right instruments."
"This is the only compliment I stock. It is also a receipt."
goodLines: "A respectable claim. The ledger will say so, which is more than the demo said."
poorLines: "The assayer files your claim under PROSPECTIVE."
